messages.subject: Re: Dependency issues with Rattle 2.6.20 on Windows and R 2.15.1
messages.subject_clean: Dependency issues with Rattle 2.6.20 on Windows and R 2.15.1
messages.body_plain:
Hi Paul,

Rattle tries to capture some dependency issues and assists by suggesting package installations as it finds packages it uses that are missing, but the issues you note seem to be second order dependencies.

I wonder if the following would fix the issue for you:

> install.packages("rattle", dependencies=TRUE)

That should install all packages and their dependencies, recursively.

Regards,
Graham

On 31 July 2012 15:14, Paul Kennedy <paul...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
>
> We're installing the latest version of Rattle but have run into dependency issues around ROC curves and ctrees. Is anyone else getting these kinds of problems?
>
> Some of the kinds of issues we see are:
> - when we open the example weather dataset, build a random forest with default settings then show the ROC, we get an empty window and an error on the console saying that a package (sorry I forget which one) cannot be loaded. I install the package and everything is ok.
> - I update all packages.
> - then I build a decision tree on the same dataset. I select "Conditional" and execute, but an error appears on the console saying that ctree can't be executed. I install the party package (where it appears) and try again and it works.
> - then I try to plot ROC graphs for both classifiers from the Evaluate tab and again get an error message on the console.
>
> It seems like there are dependency issues, and I suspect it's probably something to do with our install, but was wondering whether anyone else had come across these kinds of problems before I reinstall both R and Rattle.
>
> Regards,
> Paul.
>

messages.subject: forests confusion matrix in rattle book
messages.subject_clean: forests confusion matrix in rattle book
messages.body_plain:
On 23 July 2012 17:28, senne <jon...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I'm reading the excellent book and thank Mr Williams for the efforts. I have a question about confusion matrix, in page 251:' model predict yes and observation was no for 26 observations', but on page 253 ' better than 26 days out of 41 days on which we'll end up wet', if 251 is true , that means 26 is false positive, aka no rain actually, how come in 253 we're wet? am I confused by this confusion matrix? thanks

Thanks for pointing out the typo. On page 251 the sentences before the one you quote are correct, and then the one you identify is incorrect. It should have the 'Yes' and 'No' swapped, to read: "That is, the model predicts No and the observation was Yes for 26 observations." That is, there are 26 false negatives (rather than false positives).

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: Translation
messages.body_plain:
A good place to start is to take the English "translation" file and work though that, replacing the msgstr parts with Portuguese:

https://code.google.com/p/rattle/source/browse/trunk/po/R-en.po

It is quite a task - not everything need be translated at once (its a big task).

You can then send it to me and I'll put it into the code repository.

Regards,
Graham
